questions.q: To generate an automatic Table of Contents, the document's headings must first be formatted with:
questions.solution: The TOC engine reads Heading 1-3 styles (and custom TOC styles). Manually bolded text carries no outline level, so it is ignored.
questions.shortcut: 'No style, no TOC' - the styles gallery, not formatting, feeds the TOC.

questions.q: VLOOKUP searches for the lookup value in which part of the table array?
questions.solution: VLOOKUP scans the first (leftmost) column of the table vertically and returns a value from the chosen column of the matching row. Searching along the first row is HLOOKUP.
questions.shortcut: V = Vertical = first column; H = Horizontal = first row.

questions.q: A file is selected in File Explorer. Pressing Alt+Enter will:
questions.solution: Alt+Enter opens the Properties dialog (size, location, dates, attributes). Enter opens the file, F2 renames it and Delete sends it to the Recycle Bin.

questions.q: The Wi-Fi wireless LAN standard family is designated by IEEE:
questions.solution: IEEE 802.11 covers Wi-Fi (a/b/g/n/ac/ax). 802.3 is wired Ethernet, 802.15 Bluetooth/PAN, 802.16 WiMAX.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: **Runs** is an action verb, so it is described by an adverb: runs very **smoothly**. (Part 3's 'hardly' is correct — a hidden negative fits here.)

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (4).
questions.solution: 'Ravi ___ him a bucket of his own the very next day' — no bucket has been mentioned before, so it is a first mention, one of many: **A** bucket. *The* would claim a known, specific bucket; *An* fails before the consonant sound; *Some* does not fit a counted single gift.
questions.shortcut: First mention, one of many → a/an; sound decides a vs an.
questions.passage: Every morning before his duty, Ravi, a city bus driver, spends an hour in his small garden behind the staff quarter. He grows tomatoes in paint buckets because the soil in his yard (1) ______ too rocky for beds. His neighbours at first (2) ______ fun of the buckets, but now three of them copy the idea. Ravi says gardening has taught him (3) ______ patient, and patience is what city traffic demands. When a passenger once praised the chillies he carried in his bag, Ravi (4) ______ him a bucket of his own the very next day.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: For **two** people the reciprocal is **each other**: 'borrowed **each other's** notes'. 'One another' is reserved for more than two.
questions.shortcut: two → each other; many → one another.

questions.q: According to the passage, why is night-time heat considered especially harmful?
options: Outdoor workers cannot complete their shifts at night
The body carries out its repair processes during sleep
Air conditioners stop working after sunset
Hospitals admit only night-time patients during heat waves
questions.solution: The passage states: 'Night-time heat is particularly dangerous because sleep is when the body repairs itself; hospitals report more admissions during hot nights...' — (b) restates the stated reason. (a) describes a para-2 problem about *day* shifts of workers, not nights. (c) is never said — the passage says the poor cannot afford electricity. (d) distorts the point about admissions being higher, not restricted, at night.
questions.shortcut: Anchor 'sleep' in para 2 and read the sentence — the answer is inside the 'because' clause.
questions.passage:
Cities are quietly getting hotter than the countryside that surrounds them, and the gap is measured every night. On a summer evening, a village a few kilometres outside a metropolis may cool to a comfortable twenty-six degrees while the city itself still holds thirty-three. This difference, known as the urban heat island effect, arises not from global warming alone but from the way cities are built. Concrete, asphalt and brick absorb solar energy all day and release it slowly after sunset, so the city never truly cools. Fewer trees mean less shade and less of the cooling that water escaping from leaves provides. Waste heat from air conditioners, vehicles and industry adds a further burden.

The consequences fall unevenly. The poorest residents often live in dense, poorly ventilated neighbourhoods with tin roofs that turn bedrooms into ovens, and they cannot afford the electricity that cooling demands. Studies in several Indian cities have linked heat waves to falling productivity among construction and delivery workers, whose shifts rarely move to the cooler hours. Night-time heat is particularly dangerous because sleep is when the body repairs itself; hospitals report more admissions during hot nights even when the days seem tolerable.

Solutions need not wait for global action. Painting roofs white, mandating reflective materials for new construction, restoring ponds and planting street trees can lower local temperatures measurably within a single season. Ahmedabad's heat action plan, which pairs early warnings with cool-roof subsidies, has become a model studied by other developing countries. What these measures share is a simple insight: heat islands are created by design choices, and design choices can be remade. The city that planned itself into a heat trap can plan itself out of one.

questions.q: India's only active volcano, Barren Island, is located in the:
options: Bay of Bengal off the Odisha coast
questions.solution: **Barren Island** lies in the **Andaman Sea**, east of the main Andaman islands. It is India's only confirmed active volcano; Narcondam nearby is dormant.

questions.q: Which country is known as the 'Land of the Midnight Sun'?
questions.solution: **Norway** lies largely north of the Arctic Circle, where the Sun stays visible at midnight in summer. Finland is the 'Land of Thousand Lakes' and Japan the 'Land of the Rising Sun'.

questions.q: The Bhagirathi and the Alaknanda meet at which place to form the Ganga?
questions.solution: The Ganga is formed at **Devprayag** (Uttarakhand), the last of the Panch Prayag, where the **Bhagirathi** joins the **Alaknanda**. Rudraprayag is the Alaknanda–Mandakini confluence; Karnaprayag is the Alaknanda–Pindar confluence.
questions.shortcut: 'Very Nice Kids Read Daily' — D = Devprayag, the final meeting.

questions.q: Which of the following rivers flows westward through a rift valley and drains into the Arabian Sea?
questions.solution: The **Narmada** rises at **Amarkantak** and flows **west** between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges in a **rift valley**, entering the **Gulf of Khambhat** (Arabian Sea) through an estuary. The other three flow east into the Bay of Bengal and form deltas.

questions.q: What approximate value will come in place of '?': $42.05\% \text{ of } 699.85 + 58.1\% \text{ of } 400.2 = \ ?$
The value of $\sin30^\circ+\cos60^\circ+\cot45^\circ$ is:
A six-digit number is formed by writing a three-digit number twice (for example 257257). Such a number is always divisible by:
questions.solution: $abcabc = abc \times 1000 + abc = abc \times 1001$ and $1001 = 7 \times 11 \times 13$. So it is always divisible by 7, 11 and 13.

questions.q: If $\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{x}{225}} = \dfrac{16}{15}$, what is the value of $x$?

**Statements:** Only a few roads are wide. All wide roads are smooth.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some roads are smooth.
II. All roads being smooth is a possibility.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
questions.solution: I: the road-that-is-wide is smooth → follows. II: draw all roads inside smooth (wide roads already are; non-wide roads join) → consistent → follows. **Both.**
questions.shortcut: A possibility passes as long as no guaranteed member collides with it.

questions.q: **In the evening, Kiran's shadow falls exactly behind her. Which direction is she facing?**
questions.solution: Evening shadows point **East**. The shadow is behind her, so she faces the opposite → **West**.
questions.shortcut: Evening: shadow East; behind → face West.

questions.q: Which set of signs will make **72 ? 8 ? 3 ? 5 ? 2 = 37** correct?
questions.solution:
Put each option's signs into the blanks from left to right, then use BODMAS:

- ÷, ×, +, ×: 72 ÷ 8 × 3 + 5 × 2 = 37 ✓
- ÷, +, ×, −: 72 ÷ 8 + 3 × 5 − 2 = 22 ✗
- ÷, ×, −, +: 72 ÷ 8 × 3 − 5 + 2 = 24 ✗
- ×, ÷, +, −: 72 × 8 ÷ 3 + 5 − 2 = 195 ✗

Only **÷, ×, +, ×** balances.
questions.shortcut: Check the target size first: a big right side needs ×; a small one needs ÷ or −.

questions.q:
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

**1, 2, 6, 15, 31, ?**
questions.shortcut: When the difference row is 1, 4, 9, 16, add the next square.
